questions.q: What does CREATE ROLE reporting_reader do by itself, before any GRANT statements run?
options: Creates a role with no permissions at all
Creates a role with the same permissions as db_datareader
Creates a role with sysadmin rights
Creates a new server login
questions.explain: CREATE ROLE only defines the role; it starts with zero permissions until you explicitly GRANT (or DENY) something to it.

questions.q: A user belongs to two roles: one grants SELECT on a table, the other has an explicit DENY SELECT on that same table. Can the user read it?
options: No — DENY always overrides any GRANT, regardless of source
Yes — GRANT and DENY cancel out, defaulting to allow
It depends on which role was created first
Yes, because GRANT was issued in a different role
questions.explain: DENY is an explicit block that wins over any GRANT the principal has through any role or direct grant.

questions.q: What does REVOKE do, as distinct from DENY?
options: It removes a previously granted or denied permission, returning to no explicit statement either way
It explicitly blocks a permission regardless of other grants
It grants a permission
It drops the role entirely
questions.explain: REVOKE clears an existing GRANT or DENY, leaving the principal with no explicit permission statement on that object (access then falls back to other applicable grants/denies, if any).

questions.q: Why is a custom role like reporting_reader preferable to db_datareader when an application only needs to read a few tables?
options: Because db_datareader grants SELECT on every table in the database, which is broader access than the job needs
Because db_datareader doesn't support SELECT at all
Because custom roles automatically expire after 90 days
Because db_datareader can only be used by sysadmin members
questions.explain: db_datareader is database-wide; a custom role can be scoped to exactly the schema, tables, or even columns the job actually needs — the practical expression of least privilege.

questions.q: Which statement correctly adds an existing user to a custom role?
options: ALTER ROLE reporting_reader ADD MEMBER app_reader;
GRANT reporting_reader TO app_reader;
CREATE USER app_reader IN ROLE reporting_reader;
ALTER LOGIN app_reader ADD ROLE reporting_reader;
questions.explain: ALTER ROLE ... ADD MEMBER is the correct syntax for adding a database user to a role.
